title: Lf^* K ⊗^L Lf^* L is a left derived bifunctor
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] and $f\colon X\to Y$ a morphism of schemes. Write $\Mod_{\Lambda_T}$ for module objects over the pulled-back ring on the pro-étale site of $T$, $f^*$ for the (exact, monoidal) pullback of module objects, $Lf^*$ for its left derived functor and $\otimes^L$ for the derived tensor product [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull, sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]; $Q_h\colon K(\Mod_{\Lambda_T})\to D(\Mod_{\Lambda_T})$ is the localization of the homotopy category. The bifunctor $(K,L)\mapsto Lf^*K\otimes^LLf^*L$ on $D(\Mod_{\Lambda_Y})$, with the transformation to $(A,B)\mapsto Q_h(f^*(A\otimes B))$ given by the counits of $Lf^*$ followed by the comparison of [def-sfb-upper-star-tensor-counit], is a left derived bifunctor of $(A,B)\mapsto Q_h(f^*(A\otimes B))$ with respect to quasi-isomorphisms in both variables.

proof.text: Transport flatness from inverseImageModule_preservesFlat along extension of scalars through the coefficient-ring isomorphism.

Apply the existing two-variable left-derivability criterion using complexes whose images under pullback are K-flat. The derived counits are isomorphisms since pullback is exact; the localization tensorator is an isomorphism on a K-flat second variable; the ordinary homotopy comparison is an isomorphism. Their composite is exactly the displayed right counit. Thus the prescribed bifunctor and counit satisfy the total left derived universal property. Identify the displayed ordinary complex comparison with the canonical cochain tensor isomorphism by extensionality in each degree and the existing coproduct formula. Compose the four component isomorphism proofs explicitly.
